speech.title: Gorodki
speech.text: Gorodki is one of the oldest Russian games. Players stand at a certain distance from a square marked on the ground and throw a heavy wooden bat at small wooden pieces called “gorodki”. The aim is to knock all the pieces out of the square in as few throws as possible. The game looks simple, but it demands a good eye, a strong arm and a lot of practice. For centuries, gorodki was played in villages and city yards by people of all ages. Today clubs hold regular competitions, and some parks have special courts for the game. For many Russians, gorodki is not just a sport but a living part of their cultural heritage.

speech.title: Lapta
speech.text: Lapta is a traditional Russian bat-and-ball game that is often compared to baseball. Two teams take turns: one team hits the ball with a wooden bat and tries to run across the field and back, while the other team tries to catch the ball or hit the runner with it. In the past, lapta was especially popular in villages, where people played it on holidays and at family gatherings. The game develops speed, quick reactions and, above all, teamwork, because no player can win alone. Although lapta is less famous today, enthusiasts organise tournaments and teach the game to children, helping to keep this old tradition alive.

speech.title: Sambo
speech.text: Sambo is a martial art that was developed in the Soviet Union in the 1920s and 1930s. Its name is short for the Russian words meaning “self-defence without weapons”. Sambo combines techniques from judo, wrestling and several traditional fighting styles, and it is based on throws, holds and quick reactions. At first it was used to train soldiers, but soon it became a sport with its own rules and championships. Today sambo is practised in many countries. It helps people become stronger and more flexible, but it also teaches discipline, respect for the opponent and self-control.

speech.title: A young figure skater
speech.text: Kamila Valieva is a Russian figure skater who was born in Kazan in 2006. She started skating as a small child and soon impressed her coaches with her flexibility, elegance and excellent technique. In 2022 she won the European Championships and became famous for performing quadruple jumps, which very few women in the world can land. Her career has already seen both great victories and serious challenges. For many young skaters, her story shows how much hard work, patience and determination it takes to reach the top in sport.
